newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi corn, wheat progress behind year ago.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi corn, wheat progress behind year ago.

text.p: Mississippi's corn planting and wheat growth remained behind last year's due to wet spring weather but conditions were improving in the week ended March 23, the Mississippi State Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly update.
Corn acreage was about 6 percent planted, down from 30 percent a year earlier and 16 pct on the 5-year average.
Wheat was 37 percent jointed, against 58 percent at the same time a year ago and 47 pct on a five-year average.
The winter wheat crop was rated 5 percent excellent, 45 pct good, 34 pct fair, 16 pct poor and nil very poor.
Cattle and pastures were in mostly good to fair condition, but 20 percent of pastures were rated poor or very poor.
Feedgrain supplies were rated 11 percent short, 83 percent adequate and 6 percent surplus.
